title: Idempotent billing pipeline: deduping inflight retries and at-least-once ingestion
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Customers and internal tests have surfaced sporadic duplicated usage charges when clients retry requests under transient network failures or when our ingestion pipeline replays messages. Root cause analysis shows multiple duplicate counter increments across the frontend API, ingestion queue, and the metering aggregator when at-least-once semantics collide with short dedupe windows and inconsistent idempotency key handling. This ticket defines a cross-stack design and implementation plan to ensure billing and quota accounting are idempotent even with retries, transient timeouts, and eventual ingestion replays.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No user-visible duplicate token/embedding charges after 72h for any retried request pattern exercised by test harness
2) Quota enforcement (per-customer, per-route) does not undercount or overcount when concurrent retries occur
3) Rate limiter metrics remain accurate and do not double-count retried requests
4) Rollout includes backstop reconciler to correct historical duplicates in case of migration bugs
5) New telemetry surfaces idempotency key hit/miss rates and dedupe effectiveness
design_decision: We will implement a two-layer deduplication model: client-supplied idempotency key (optional but recommended) validated at edge + server-managed canonicalization and a short-lived durable dedupe store keyed by (customer_id, idempotency_key or request_fingerprint, model_variant, route). The ingestion pipeline (Kafka consumer -> metering service) will perform best-effort dedupe using the same canonical key and a monotonic sequence where available. For at-least-once replay windows, the aggregator will rely on append-only idempotent writes to the billing ledger (SQL upsert with dedupe token) and an async reconciler that detects and fixes remaining duplicates. We will limit dedupe TTL to 24 hours for memory/disk budget, and provide an optional extended dedupe for enterprise customers via Reserved Capacity retention rules.
alternatives_considered: A) Stateless heuristics only: fingerprinting request payloads at the edge - rejected because false positives on semantically equivalent prompts and inability to reconcile replays
B) Full end-to-end exactly-once by changing transport to transactional write-through to ledger - rejected for rollout risk and performance impact
C) Client-only idempotency requirement - rejected because many third-party SDKs and internal components don't send keys reliably
implementation_tasks: 1. API: add Idempotency-Key header validation and canonicalization in gateway (ENG-GW-202).
2. Gateway: persist idempotency key + fingerprint to short-lived dedupe store (Redis with LRU + bounded TTL).
3. Ingestion: enhance Kafka consumer to attach dedupe-key to messages and skip processing for known keys.
4. Metering service: change writes to billing ledger to upsert on dedupe token and emit 'dedupe_hit' telemetry.
5. Reconciler: implement async job to scan recent ledger and remove duplicate invoice rows; expose manual run for support.
6. QA: create load test harness that simulates retries, network partitions, and Kafka replays.
7. Docs/SDK: publish SDK guidance and convenience header helper for clients.
8. Rollout: feature flag behind 'billing-idempotency-v1' with gradual ramp and canary customers.
9. Migration: one-time backfill script to mark currently counted events with dedupe tokens where possible.
10. Security review: verify dedupe store access patterns and encryption at rest for dedupe keys containing PII.
11. Infra: capacity sizing for Redis dedupe store and benchmarking for write QPS under peak load.
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization and fingerprint generation
Integration test that replays identical messages and asserts single ledger row
Chaos test: cut connections between gateway and dedupe store and assert eventual correctness
Load test with 10k concurrent retries per second to validate performance and failover
Regression test ensuring rate limiter counters are incremented exactly once per effective request
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Deploy API + dedupe-store in non-production and run automated replay tests
Phase 1: Enable for 5% of traffic with feature flag, monitor dedupe_hit, charge anomalies
Phase 2: Canary on low-traffic customers for 48h, run reconciliation and validate billing reports
Phase 3: Gradually ramp to 100% over 72h, keep reconciliation running in background
Phase 4: Offer extended dedupe TTL for Reserved Capacity customers and update billing docs
monitoring_and_telemetry: metric: billing.dedupe.hits per customer, route, model_variant
trace: sample trace id annotated with dedupe_decision and source component
alert: sudden drop in dedupe_hit rate or spike in duplicate invoice creation
dashboard: dedupe effectiveness and per-customer reconciler actions
updates: 2026-02-26: Triage completed; priority set to P0 after customer-reported double-charging incident.
2026-03-01: Design review with payments and infra - decided on two-layer dedupe and reconciler approach.
2026-03-04: Prototype Redis-based dedupe store implemented and benchmarked for 15k ops/s.
2026-03-09: Security review requested; flagged potential PII in idempotency keys — using HMAC canonicalization to mitigate.
2026-03-12: End-to-end tests passing in staging; found race with concurrent consumer group commits, adding consumer-side dedupe check.
2026-03-14: Rolling feature-flag gated canary deployment to 5% of traffic; monitoring dashboards created.
